cases.text:
Handoff notes between agent sessions (from a colleague's team notes, September 2026)

We stopped asking agents to summarise the whole session at the end. Instead each session keeps a short handoff file with three parts: the goal, what is done, and what is next with the exact file to open first. The next session reads it before its first reply. Over six weeks the team counted how often a new session repeated work the last one had finished: it fell from about one session in four to one in fifteen. The handoff file stays under a page; longer notes go into dated journals that nobody reads by default. The failure we still see is a handoff that says what was done but not what was decided, so the next session re-opens a settled question.

cases.text:
Trimming tool results before an agent reads them (from a colleague's team notes, October 2026)

Tool result trimming means cutting what a tool returns down to the part the next step needs, before it goes back into the agent's context. Our search tool used to return forty hits with full snippets; the agent read them all and lost track of the question. We now keep the top five hits, cap each snippet at two sentences, and put the count of dropped hits on the last line so the agent knows more exists. Over two weeks the number of runs that ended on the wrong file fell from about one in six to one in twenty. The cost is a second call when the first five hits miss, which happened in roughly one run in ten.

cases.text:
Reserving context budget for the plan in a long-running agent (from a colleague's team notes, October 2026)

Our coding agent runs sessions of several hundred tool calls, and for months its plan was the first thing the language model forgot: as tool results filled the context window, the plan at the top was trimmed or ignored, and the agent drifted into side tasks. We now reserve a fixed share of the context window for the plan and the current step, about one tenth, and let tool results and chat history share the rest. When the rest fills up, the oldest tool results are dropped first and the plan is never cut. Across 200 sessions the number of runs that ended on a task nobody asked for fell from about one in five to one in twenty. The cost is that very large tool results are cut earlier than before, so the agent sometimes has to call the same tool a second time.
cases.author: eval-case-writer

cases.text:
Reusing tool results inside one agent run (from a colleague's team notes, October 2026)

A tool-using language-model agent often asks the same question of the same tool twice in one run: it lists a folder, reads a file, then lists the folder again after an unrelated step. We added a small cache inside each run that stores a tool call's arguments and its result, and serves the stored result when the same call repeats and nothing the call depends on has changed. Over 300 runs the number of tool calls per run fell by about a fifth and the agent's context filled more slowly. The cache is thrown away when the run ends, because a result kept across runs went stale and produced confident wrong answers. The open problem is deciding when a write by the agent should invalidate a cached read, which we still do by a hand-kept list of tools that change state.
